description: Policy for the AI RMF questionnaire at engagement time. build_ai_questions.py gives each subcategory a question type per bank from the usage profile (runs/<Org>_<date>/ai_usage.json), then selects candidates with the filters and ranking below. Change policy by editing this file, not the code. The type is set at topic level: the CSF tool already assesses general security (and the ISO 27001 SoA), so with a CSF assessment done or ISO 27001 held the AI RMF questionnaire only asks the AI angle of data, infrastructure and access topics.

no_effect_flags.iso42001_held: ISO/IEC 42001 held: not used to relax any question type until the AI RMF to 42001 crosswalk is verified; everything stays full_discovery

ai_area_rules.description: Which AI areas (data/ai/ai_areas.json) a client gets, besides the ones ticked in the intake menus ai_usage and ai_components: always, any_ai (AI in use), role (the answer to "Do you build AI, use AI, or both?") and with (an area that brings others). Every AI area must be reachable (a test checks it).

legacy_profile.description: Until question selection works on AI areas (TODO step 4), intake.py also writes the old profile fields, worked out from the AI areas with these tables. Removed in step 4.

none.skip_reason: No AI use declared: not applicable
none.live_reason: No AI use declared; the unsanctioned-use check stays live

unsure.reason: AI use unconfirmed: scoped as consumer, base rung; discovery of what AI is in use comes first

reasons.gap: {flags} covers general security; this topic ({topic}) asks only what differs for AI
reasons.default: No CSF assessment or ISO 27001 for the {topic} topic: full discovery
reasons.forced: Forced to full discovery for an unconfirmed AI profile

gap_frame: General security controls ({flags}) already cover the standard aspects of this area. What differs for AI: {text}
review_flag: LOW — bank entry flagged for human review; assessor verification required
